title: Event Delegation Matcher
subtopicTitle: DOM Event Flow: Capturing, Bubbling & Delegation
problemStatement: Implement `delegate(container, selector, eventType, handler)` that listens on `container` and triggers `handler(e, matchedElement)` only when the event originates from or bubbles through an element matching `selector`.
interviewTrap: Directly checking `event.target.matches(selector)` fails if the user clicks a nested child (like an `<i>` or `<span>` inside a `<button>`). Using `.closest()` is required.

testCases.name: Triggers handler when child matches selector
testCases.testFn: const parent = document.createElement('div'); const btn = document.createElement('button'); btn.id = 'btn-1'; btn.className = 'action-btn'; parent.appendChild(btn); let clickedId = ''; const listener = delegate(parent, '.action-btn', (e, el) => { clickedId = el.id; }); listener({ target: btn }); return clickedId;

testCases.name: Triggers handler when clicking deeply nested child inside matching element
testCases.testFn: const parent = document.createElement('div'); const btn = document.createElement('button'); btn.id = 'btn-2'; btn.className = 'action-btn'; const span = document.createElement('span'); btn.appendChild(span); parent.appendChild(btn); let clickedId = ''; const listener = delegate(parent, '.action-btn', (e, el) => { clickedId = el.id; }); listener({ target: span }); return clickedId;

testCases.name: Ignores clicks outside selector
testCases.testFn: const parent = document.createElement('div'); const div = document.createElement('div'); parent.appendChild(div); let called = false; const listener = delegate(parent, '.action-btn', () => { called = true; }); listener({ target: div }); return called;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Events travel down from `window` through the DOM tree (Capturing Phase) until they reach the target (Target Phase), then bubble back up to `window` (Bubbling Phase). Event delegation attaches a single listener to a common ancestor, querying `event.target.closest()`.

3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Event Delegation & Target Traversal is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is Event Delegation and why is it memory efficient?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Event Delegation attaches a single event listener to a common parent element rather than attaching separate listeners to hundreds of child elements. It leverages the Event Bubbling phase: events originating on children bubble up to the parent, where `event.target` identifies the originating element. It drastically reduces memory footprint and automatically handles dynamically added children without re-binding.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between event.target and event.currentTarget?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `event.target` is the actual innermost DOM element where the event originated (the clicked button). `event.currentTarget` is the element to which the event handler is currently attached (the parent listener). In event delegation, `target` is the child, `currentTarget` is the parent.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Essential distinction for DOM event programming.

realWorldUseCases.description: Attaching a single click handler to a 10,000-row table instead of attaching 10,000 individual event listeners.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: table.addEventListener('click', e => { const row = e.target.closest('tr'); if (row) handleRow(row); });

howToExplain.opening: Event delegation harnesses the DOM event bubbling mechanism to handle events at a parent container level, optimizing memory and simplifying dynamic element handling.
keyPoints: Attaches one listener to parent instead of N listeners to children.
event.target points to clicked element; event.currentTarget points to listener element.
Uses Element.closest() to resolve target matching nested child spans or icons.
Automatically handles dynamically inserted or deleted child nodes.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Event delegation is the primary technique for maintaining lightweight DOM memory profiles in high-density web apps.
analogies: A company reception desk: one receptionist signs for all incoming packages rather than delivery drivers wandering to every employee desk.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using e.target.matches('button') when buttons contain inner <span> or <svg> elements.
commonMistakes.why: Clicking the icon makes e.target the svg, causing matches('button') to return false.
commonMistakes.correct: Use `e.target.closest('button')` to walk up to the button container.

followUpDeepDive.question: Which DOM events do NOT bubble?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `focus`, `blur`, `load`, `unload`, `mouseenter`, and `mouseleave` do NOT bubble. However, `focusin` and `focusout` do bubble and can be delegated.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: W3C UI Events Specification §3.1 Event dispatch and DOM tree
